description: decide.py has no de-duplication / idempotency guard against repeatedly recording the same open paper signal. Every invocation that finds a positive-edge side unconditionally appends a NEW row to the ledger (decide.py:89-96), with no check for an already-open position on the same token_id/market from a prior pass. If run.sh is invoked repeatedly (e.g. cron every few minutes) while a sustained BTC momentum window keeps producing a positive edge, the ledger will accumulate multiple duplicate 'open' rows representing the same underlying signal rather than one position tracked to resolution, inflating the paper-trade count without adding distinct trading decisions. This compounds FIND-001 (there is also no resolution step at all yet) but is a separate, independent gap: even once resolution exists, this write path would still need a same-market open-position check to avoid unbounded duplicate stacking.
